papers.title: Dual-target chemical profiling of anti-influenza multi-components from Isatidis Radix via direct binding to neuraminidase and hemagglutinin.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Yang Z, Yang P, Wu F, Wang Y, Wu T et al.
papers.abstract: Isatidis Radix, the root of Isatis indigotica, is a traditional Chinese medicine used against influenza. However, its chemical profile responsible for direct anti-influenza activity remains poorly characterized. This present study aims to classify the anti-influenza constituents of Isatidis Radix and to investigate their direct interactions with the key viral targets, neuraminidase (NA) and hemagglutinin (HA). To this end, a compound library comprising 91 constituents was assembled (78 isolated and 13 acquired), including nine undescribed compounds. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was employed to assess binding affinities to NA and HA. Antiviral activity of the compound library was validated in influenza A (H1N1)-infected A549 cells, and molecular docking simulations were performed to explore binding modes. SPR screening revealed that 63.7% and 71.4% of the library showed moderate-to-strong binding to NA and HA, respectively, with alkaloids and lignans as the predominant active classes. Notably, compounds 8, 15, 48, and 87 exhibited nanomolar KD values (0.49-4.22 nM for NA; 0.63-6.26 nM for HA), comparable to oseltamivir and arbidol. Cellular assays demonstrated that 76.9% of tested compounds showed antiviral activity (EC50 < 200 μM), with indole alkaloids and glycosylated lignans being most potent. Integrative SPR and cellular data confirmed a positive correlation between dual-target binding and antiviral efficacy. These findings establish that the anti-influenza activity of Isatidis Radix arises from multi-component, multi-target actions on NA and HA, providing a scientific basis for its clinical use and quality control.

papers.title: [Effects of the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 on the growth and rhizosphere environment of Astragalus membranaceus var. mongholicus].
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.authors: Lu G, Zhang S, Wang Y, Shi Z, Niu J, Liang J
papers.abstract: Plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) play an important role in promoting plant growth and improving soil environment. This is particularly relevant in the context of the current high-quality development of the traditional Chinese medicine industry, where the application of PGPR in the cultivation of medicinal plants contributes to ensuring the quality and safety of medicinal materials and promoting sustainable and high-quality industrial development. In this study, Astragalus membranaceus var. mongholicus was used as the object to explore the effects of nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 soaking on the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus seedlings, rhizosphere soil nutrients and enzyme activities, bacterial community structure and assembly mechanism, in order to reveal its growth-promoting mechanism. Therefore, the seeds of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus were inoculated with the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 via seed soaking prior to sowing. After 60 days of growth, the seedlings and rhizosphere soil samples were collected. Seedling growth indices, soil nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium content, as well as soil enzyme activities were determined. A soil microbial library was constructed using 16S rDNA gene sequencing, followed by taxonomic annotation and diversity analysis to compare the differences in species composition among groups. The microbial community assembly process was elucidated using infer community assembly mechanisms by phylogenetic-bin-based null model analysis (iCAMP). The relationship between soil redundancy analysis (RDA), and a species co-occurrence network was constructed. The metabolic functional potential of the microbial community was predicted using PICRUSt2 (phylogenetic investigation of communities by reconstruction of unobserved states). The results showed that inoculation with the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 promoted the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus and improved the soil quality. Compared with the control, the root length, shoot dry weight and root dry weight increased by 32.08%, 64.56% and 84.36%, respectively, while the soil alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen content, available phosphorus, and soil urease activity increased by 134.09%, 27.00% and 136.39%, respectively. Furthermore, the strain T4 altered the soil bacterial community structure, driving a shift in community assembly from stochastic processes to deterministic processes, and significantly enriched functional bacterial genera such as Arthrobacter, Acinetobacter and Mesorhizobium (P<0.05). Functional prediction showed that the metabolic functions of the microbial community were significantly enhanced in four aspects (P<0.05): reduction in nitrogen loss, enhancement of detoxification capacity, induction of plant resistance, and augmentation of microbial vitality. In summary, the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 promoted the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus by regulating the rhizosphere microecology and improving soil quality. It lays a theoretical and application foundation for the development of special bacterial fertilizer that can effectively improve soil nutrition level and promote the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus.

papers.title: [Research progress on the multi-target modulation of signaling pathways by acupuncture in the treatment of obesity].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Qu W, Jiang Q, Wei D, Zheng X, Zhu M, Liang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a complex metabolic disorder induced by multiple factors, including genetics, environment, and lifestyle. The pathogenesis involves dysregulated glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin and leptin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and abnormal fat accumulation. These alterations are closely associated with aberrant regulation of key signaling pathways such as adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK2/STAT3), Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor κB (TLR4/NF-κB), and silent information regulator 1 (SIRT1) signaling network. As a multi-target intervention method, acupuncture therapy has made significant progress in recent years in improving obesity-related pathological conditions and signaling pathway imbalances. This article reviews the regulatory effects of acupuncture on signaling pathways such as AMPK, JAK2/STAT3, TLR4/NF-κB, and SIRT1 signaling network, explores its molecular mechanism of action in improving obesity, and provides a scientific theoretical basis for the clinical application of acupuncture therapy and the optimization of individual weight-loss strategies.

papers.title: [Analysis of the patterns and characteristics of enhanced efficacy and reduced toxicity of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Yang N, Liu Y, Liu C
papers.abstract: Monotherapy often falls short in treating complex diseases effectively, prompting the emergence of integrated treatment models such as acupuncture-medicine combination therapy, which has gained recognition as a significant strategy to improve clinical efficacy while minimizing adverse effects. This paper systematically examines the necessity of integrating acupuncture with pharmacotherapy. By constructing a theoretical framework centered on supplementation and regulation, it delineates the operational principles of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy. It explores the mechanisms underlying the enhanced efficacy of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy from the perspectives of synergy and complementarity, and analyzes its characteristics in toxicity reduction via counteracting mechanisms. The aim of this paper is to provide a theoretical foundation and future directions for research on acupuncture-medicine combination therapy.

papers.title: [Secondary temperature rise effect at Guanyuan (CV4) after moxibustion in patients with primary dysmenorrhea and its influence on therapeutic effect].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Xu W, Xie D, Li H, Chen R
papers.abstract:
To observe the secondary temperature rise effect at Guanyuan (CV4) induced by moxibustion and its correlation with therapeutic efficacy in patients with primary dysmenorrhea (PD).
A total of 170 PD patients were divided into a non-deqi group (n=61) and a deqi group (n=109) according to the presence or absence of deqi sensation during moxibustion at CV4. After propensity score matching, 59 patients were included in each group. All patients received suspended moxibustion at CV4 for 30 min. Skin temperature at CV4 was measured before and after moxibustion. The presence or absence of secondary temperature rise effect after cessation of moxibustion was observed in both groups. Differences in effective deqi time, deqi intensity, and deqi dimensions were compared between patients with and without secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group. Subsequently, patients in the deqi group received moxibustion treatment for 2 menstrual cycles, with (7±2) days of treatment per menstrual cycle. The short-form McGill pain questionnaire (SF-MPQ) and COX menstrual symptom scale (CMSS) were used to evaluate the influence of secondary temperature rise effect on therapeutic efficacy.
The incidence of secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group was 59.32% (35/59), which was significantly higher than 3.39% (2/59) in the non-deqi group (P<0.01). In patients with secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group, the mean degree of secondary temperature rise was (0.54±0.13) ℃, and the peak of secondary temperature rise appeared at (22.06±1.66) min after cessation of moxibustion. The cooling trend after secondary temperature rise was slower than that immediately after moxibustion (P<0.01). Compared with patients without secondary temperature rise effect, those with secondary temperature rise effect had longer effective deqi time (P<0.01), stronger deqi intensity (P<0.01), and higher incidence rates of general comfort emotional experience and autonomic response dimensions (P<0.01). The degree of secondary temperature rise was positively correlated with effective deqi time and deqi intensity (P<0.001). After treatment and at follow-up, SF-MPQ and CMSS scores in both patients with and without secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group were lower than those before treatment (P<0.01), and scores in patients with secondary temperature rise effect were lower than those in patients without secondary temperature rise effect (P<0.05, P<0.01). The total effective rate was 95.83% (23/24) in patients with secondary temperature rise effect, which was higher than 75.00% (18/24) in patients without secondary temperature rise effect (P<0.05). The degree of secondary temperature rise was positively correlated with therapeutic efficacy (P<0.001).
Moxibustion at CV4 can induce a secondary temperature rise effect after deqi, which is closely related to effective deqi time, deqi intensity, and deqi dimensions. The secondary temperature rise effect at CV4 can further improve the clinical efficacy in PD patients, and a higher degree of secondary temperature rise is associated with better therapeutic effect.

papers.title: [Study on regulatory effects of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Feng T, Li J, Jia Y, Tao Y, Xu J
papers.abstract:
To investigate the effect of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), and to compare its efficacy with that of mild moxibustion.
Forty-eight Wistar rats were randomly assigned to 4 groups (n=12):normal, model, mild moxibustion, and warm needling. KOA was induced by intra-articular injection of monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) into the right knee. Rats in the mild moxibustion and warm needling moxibustion groups received interventions at the acupoints "Futu" (ST32) and "Zusanli" (ST36), 30 min per session, once every other day for 4 weeks. After intervention, Lequesne MG scores, the right knee joint horizontal diameter, and right hind paw pain threshold were assessed. Histopathological changes in the rat knee joints were observed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) and safranin O staining, and were scored using the Mankin's and OARSI systems. Serum contents of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-18 (IL-18), and matrix metalloproteinase-13 (MMP-13) were measured by ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, MMP-13, and type Ⅱ collagen (Collagen-Ⅱ) in knee cartilage. Western blot was performed to detect the relative protein expression levels of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, Collagen-Ⅱ, IL-6, and MMP-13 in cartilage tissue.
Compared with the normal group, the model group showed a significantly higher Lequesne MG score (P<0.01), an increased horizontal diameter of the right knee joint (P<0.01), and a decreased pain threshold (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups exhibited significantly lower Lequesne MG scores (P<0.01), reduced joint horizontal diameters (P<0.01), and increased pain thresholds (P<0.01). Compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group showed a lower Lequesne MG score (P<0.01) and a higher pain threshold (P<0.01). Histopathological staining revealed degenerative features in the model group, including damage to the superficial cartilage layer and disappearance of the tidemark, while both treatment groups exhibited milder degeneration. Compared with the normal group, both the Mankin's and OARSI scores were significantly increased in the model group (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both scores were decreased in the mild moxibustion and warm needling groups (P<0.01), and the scores in the warm needling group were significantly lower than those in the mild moxibustion group (P<0.05). Compared with the normal group, the serum contents of IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 were significantly elevated in the model group (P<0.01);in cartilage tissue, the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins were increased (P<0.01), while Collagen-Ⅱ expression was reduced (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups showed decreased serum IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 contents, and reduced expression of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins in cartilage tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05), along with increased Collagen-Ⅱ expression (P<0.01). Furthermore, compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group exhibited more significant changes in the above indicators except joint horizontal diameter (P<0.01, P<0.05).
Warm needling moxibustion effectively improves knee osteoarthritis in rats and shows superior efficacy compared with mild moxibustion. Its therapeutic mechanism may be associated with the inhibition of chondrocyte senescence.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on the SIRT1/HIF-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway of thoracic aorta in ApoE-/- atherosclerotic mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Luo Y, Hu X, Zeng Y, Zhang N
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of electroacupuncture(EA) on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress status, pathological morphology of the thoracic aorta and the expression of silent information regulator 1(SIRT1)/hypoxia-inducible factor 1α(HIF-1α)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2(Nrf2)signaling pathway in ApoE-/- atherosclerotic(AS)mice, in order to explore the potential mechanism of EA in the prevention and treatment of AS.
Ten C57BL/6J mice were assigned as the control group and fed with normal diet, while 42 SPF-grade male ApoE-/- mice were fed with high-fat diet for 12 weeks to establish an AS model. Following successful model induction, the ApoE-/- mice were randomly divided into model, EA, EA+inhibitor, and agonist groups, with 10 mice per group. The EA group received EA at the acupoints "Neiguan"(PC6), "Tongli"(HT5), and "Zusanli"(ST36) using a sparse-dense wave(2 Hz/15 Hz), with a current intensity of 0.3 mA. Each session lasted for 20 min. The EA+inhibitor group received intraperitoneal injections of the SIRT1 inhibitor EX-527(10 mg/kg), with other treatment identical to that in the EA group. The agonist group received intragastric administration of the SIRT1 agonist resveratrol(50 mg/kg). All interventions were administered every other day for 8 weeks. Body weight was measured once every 4 weeks. Serum levels of triglycerides(TG), total cholesterol(TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol(HDL-C), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol(LDL-C), as well as the oxidative stress markers superoxide dismutase(SOD), malondialdehyde(MDA), and glutathione peroxidase(GSH-Px)were measured using colorimetric assays. Histopathological changes in the aorta were assessed using hematoxylin-eosin(HE)staining. The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1, HIF-1α, and Nrf2 in the aorta were analyzed by Western blot and real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR, respectively.
After treatments, compared with the control group, the model group exhibited significantly decreased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.01), increased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.01). HE staining showed pathological changes in the vessel wall, including thickened intima with an uneven surface, proliferated endothelial cells forming plaques, inflammatory cell infiltration on the plaque surface, elastic layer structure damage, disordered arrangement of the media smooth muscle layer, and localized foam cells and smooth muscle cell proliferation. Additionally, the protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly down-regulated(P<0.01), while those of HIF-1α were up-regulated(P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both the EA and agonist groups showed increased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.01, P<0.05), decreased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.01). HE staining revealed improved endothelial morphology, with intact vascular wall, relatively smooth intima, a small amount of endothelial cells abscission, regular arrangement of the smooth muscle layer of the media, no obvious damage in the elastic layer structure, and a small amount of foam cells and smooth muscle cells proliferated.The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly increased(P<0.01, P<0.05), while HIF-1α protein and mRNA expression levels were decreased(P<0.01). Compared with the EA group, the EA+inhibitor group showed decreased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.05), increased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.05, P<0.01). HE staining showed that the structural integrity of the vascular wall was damaged, with thickening and injury of the endometrium, endothelial cell proliferation plaques and infiltration of inflammatory cells on the plaque surface, disordered arrangement of smooth muscle layer, and obvious proliferation of smooth muscle cells. The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly reduced(P<0.01, P<0.05), while those of HIF-1α were increased(P<0.01, P<0.05).
EA may regulate lipid metabolism, alleviate oxidative stress injury, promote vascular intimal repair, and delay the progression of AS in ApoE-/- mice through the activation of the SIRT1/HIF-1α/Nrf2 antioxidant signaling pathway.

papers.title: [Research progress on the autonomic-immune mechanism of acupuncture in regulating ovarian function].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Huang Y, Xu T, Li C, Yuan Y, Xia Y
papers.abstract: Ovarian dysfunction is an important cause of ovulatory disorders, infertility and endocrine disorders in women, which is commonly observed in conditions including polycystic ovary syndrome, primary ovarian insufficiency, diminished ovarian reserve and ovarian aging-related states. Recent studies have demonstrated that besides abnormalities in the classic hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, autonomic nervous imbalance and immune-inflammatory disturbance also serve as critical mechanisms underlying impaired ovarian function. Central inflammatory responses, chronic stress and metabolic abnormalities can disrupt hypothalamic rhythmic regulation, augment sympathetic nerve output and induce local chronic low-grade ovarian inflammation, consequently contributing to follicular developmental disorders and aberrant steroidogenesis. As a neuromodulation therapy initiated by somatic sensory input, acupuncture can modulate central integration via the "spinal cord-brainstem-hypothalamus" pathway, thereby regulating autonomic nervous activity and immune-inflammatory responses and improving the local ovarian microenvironment. Existing evidence suggests that acupuncture may exert its effects by inhibiting sympathetic overactivation, recruiting vagus-related anti-inflammatory pathways, modulating immune cell polarization, and alleviating oxidative stress and apoptosis. This paper reviews research progress from three aspects: the autonomic-immune regulatory basis of ovarian function, pathological imbalance characteristics, and intervention mechanisms of acupuncture, so as to provide references for neuroimmune-targeted intervention of ovarian dysfunction and acupuncture mechanism research.

papers.title: [Explanation on modern mechanism of "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated": acupuncture at Zusanli (ST36) regulates the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis" for the treatment of diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Ma J, Chen Y, Xia Y
papers.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a functional intestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea and altered defecation habits. It is frequently comorbid with psychological disorders such as anxiety and depression, which greatly impair the quality of life. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that the core pathological links of IBS-D involve disrupted brain-gut interaction and dysregulation of the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis", including visceral hypersensitivity, low-grade mucosal inflammation, impaired intestinal barrier function, gut microbiota dysbiosis and abnormal autonomic nerve modulation. Zusanli (ST36) is an essential acupoint for digestive disorders, and the ancient maxim "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated" summarizes its prominent clinical value in abdominal ailments. Modern studies have verified that acupuncture at ST36 can remodel vagal-sympathetic balance via the peripheral afferent-central integration-autonomic efferent circuit, modulate central nociceptive and emotional processing, and exert regulatory effects on brain-gut peptide signals such as 5-hydroxytryptamine, suppress immune activation and release of inflammatory mediators, improve the expression of tight-junction proteins and intestinal mucosal permeability, as well as modulate microbiota-metabolite-related pathways. Thereby, it attenuates the neuro-immune feedback of "stress-inflammation-pain amplification", alleviates visceral hypersensitivity and relieves symptoms including abdominal pain and diarrhea. Taking the classical maxim "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated" as a clue, this paper reviews research advances regarding acupuncture at ST36 in treating IBS-D by regulating the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis". Limitations of current evidence are also pointed out, including insufficient circuit verification, unclear stimulus parameter-effect relationship and non-standardized clinical protocols, so as to provide references for standardized application and mechanistic exploration of acupuncture at ST36 in treating functional gastrointestinal disorders.

papers.title: [Discussion on the closed-loop regulation strategy for acupuncture "Deqi" based on brain-computer interface and its peripheral-central mechanisms].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Yin L, Ye Y, Li Y, Luo J, Zhou H, Tian Y et al.
papers.abstract: It is held that "Deqi" is the key to the therapeutic effect of acupuncture, but its evaluation has long relied on subjective feelings and lacks objective biological indicators. In the present article, we systematically review the current research status of brain-computer interface (BCI) technology based on electroencephalogram (EEG) in analyzing the peripheral-cerebral neural mechanism of "Deqi", and further explore how to utilize the closed-loop regulation ability of BCI to actively induce and maintain the "Deqi" state. By integrating domestic and foreign literature, we analyzed the peripheral initiation mechanism and central response characteristics of "Deqi", and explored its application value of EEG-BCI in the objective identification and the construction of closed-loop feedback systems. Studies have demonstrated that EEG, with its millisecond-level time resolution, can capture the dynamic changes of neural oscillations during the "Deqi" process in real time. The feature decoding method based on machine learning further realizes the objective identification of the "Deqi" state, while the closed-loop feedback system constructed by BCI technology provides an innovative path for precise acupuncture treatment. However, this field still faces some challenges such as signal artifact interference, insufficient decoding accuracy, and inconsistent research paradigms. The deep integration of EEG-BCI with acupuncture medicine provides a key technical platform for decoding the scientific connotation of "Deqi" and active regulation. In the future, efforts should be made to develop dynamic network decoding technology, further deepen the research on peripheral-cerebral coupling mechanisms, and promote the transformation of the system towards intelligence and standardization.

papers.title: [Mechanism of electroacupuncture combined with antibiotics targeting dorsal motor nucleus of vagus nerve to activate vagus-adrenal axis, alleviate inflammatory response and reduce mortality in septic mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Liu J, Ren H, Lin Q, Zhao S, Li T, Jian H et al.
papers.abstract:
To explore the mechanism by which electroacupuncture (EA) combined with antibiotics regulates the vagus-adrenal axis via the dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV), promotes catecholamine secretion, attenuates inflammatory storm, and improves survival rate in septic mice.
Experiment 1:fifty C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into sham operation group, model group, antibiotic group, EA group, and EA + antibiotic group, with 10 mice in each group. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was performed to establish the sepsis model. Mice in the EA group received 15 min EA (10 Hz, 0.5 mA) at bilateral "Zusanli" (ST36), once daily for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the antibiotic group were intraperitoneally injected with imipenem-cilastatin sodium (30 mg/kg) every 12 h for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the EA+antibiotic group received EA and antibiotic treatment the same as the above. The 3-day survival rate and body weight changes of mice in each group were recorded. ELISA was adopted to detect serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). HE staining was used to observe pathological changes and the number of inflammatory cells in cecal tissues. Whole-brain optical clearing was performed to detect the expression of proto-oncogene c-Fos protein (c-Fos) in the DMV region. Experiment 2:fifty Chat-Cre mice were randomly assigned to sham operation + empty virus group, model + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group, with 10 mice per group. Corresponding viruses were injected into the DMV 3 weeks before model establishment. CLP operation was conducted 3 weeks after virus injection, followed by daily intraperitoneal injection of clozapine N-oxide (CNO, 3 mg/kg), combined with antibiotics or EA treatment (the same interventions and parameters as Experiment 1). Serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels were measured by ELISA;cecal inflammatory infiltration was evaluated via HE staining. Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) was applied to detect serum catecholamines including dopamine (DA), epinephrine (E), norepinephrine (NE), as well as their metabolites 3-methoxytyramine (3-MT), normetanephrine (NMN), and metanephrine (MN) levels. Immunofluorescence staining was used to quantify the counts of forkhead box protein P3 positive / cluster of differentiation 4 positive (FOXP3+/CD4+) cells in cecal tissues.
Experiment 1:compared with the sham operation group, the model group exhibited markedly decreased 3-day survival rate and body weight (P<0.000 1), elevated serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), and increased inflammatory cell infiltration in cecum (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model group, the EA + antibiotic group showed improved survival rate (P<0.05), alleviated body weight loss (P<0.000 1), decreased serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), reduced inflammatory cell infiltration (P<0.000 1), and elevated c-Fos positive cell density in DMV (P<0.000 1). Moreover, all above indicators were superior to those in the single EA or single antibiotic group to varying degrees. Experiment 2:in comparison with the sham operation + empty virus group, the model + empty virus group had higher serum inflammatory factor levels and more cecal inflammatory infiltrates (P<0.0001), and lower levels of catecholamines and their metabolites, as well as fewer FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecal tissues (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model + empty virus group, the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group displayed reduced serum inflammatory factors and relieved cecal inflammatory infiltration (P<0.000 1, P<0.01, P<0.05), accompanied by increased levels of catecholamines and metabolites, and more FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecum (P<0.01, P<0.05, P<0.001, P<0.000 1). Relative to the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, all the above indicators were reversed in the EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group (P<0.01, P<0.001, P<0.05, except for 3-MT).
EA at ST36 combined with antibiotics exerts optimal therapeutic effects on CLP-induced septic mice. The underlying mechanism may involve activating cholinergic neurons in DMV, regulating the vagus-adrenal axis to facilitate catecholamine secretion, suppressing excessive inflammatory response, and consequently elevating survival rate.
papers.title_ko: 전침과 항생제 병용이 패혈증 마우스에서 미주신경-부신 축을 통해 염증을 억제하고 생존율을 높이는 기전

summary.question: 전침과 항생제 병용이 패혈증 마우스의 생존과 염증 반응을 어떻게 개선하는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: CLP로 패혈증을 유도한 마우스와 DMV 표적 바이러스 조작 마우스를 이용해 전침, 항생제, 병용 중재 후 생존율, 염증지표, DMV c-Fos, 카테콜아민, FOXP3+/CD4+ 세포를 비교한 실험연구이다.

papers.title: [Electroacupuncture ameliorates chronic restraint stress-induced depressive-like behavior by modulating paraventricular nucleus corticotropin-releasing hormone neuron activity in mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Lin D, Li S, Huang J, Luo S, Liu J, Xue A
papers.abstract:
To investigate the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) at "Hegu" (LI4) and "Taichong" (LR3) on depressive-like behaviors and corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) neuron-related activity in paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice exposed to chronic restraint stress (CRS), so as to explore its possible mechanism.
Male C57BL/6J mice and CRH-Cre mice were used in the separate experimental cohorts of this study. A CRS-induced depressive-like behavior model was established and treated with bilateral EA at LI4 and LR3 (2 Hz, 0.5 mA, 30 min in duration of stimulation, once daily for 7 d). Behavioral changes were evaluated using forced swimming, tail suspension and open-field tests. Serum CRH, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and corticosterone (CORT) levels were measured using ELISA. The PVN neuronal activation and the proportion of c-Fos-positive cells among mCherry-labeled PVN CRH neurons were evaluated using immunofluorescence staining and c-Fos/mCherry co-labeling. Event-related PVN CRH neuron calcium activity was recorded by using fiber photometry. Chemogenetic activation with clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) was further used to observe the behavioral changes under subthreshold stress and EA intervention effect.
Compared with the blank group, the model group showed a significant increase in the immobility time in the forced swimming and tail suspension tests (P<0.01, P<0.001), distance traveled in the peripheral zone in the open-field test (P<0.001), contents of serum CRH, ACTH and CORT (P<0.000 1, P<0.001), number of c-Fos positive cell in the PVN (P<0.05), and the percentage of c-Fos/mCherry double-positive cells among the mCherry-positive cells (P<0.05). Compared with the model group, EA shortened the immobility time in the forced swimming and tail suspension tests (P<0.05), decreased the distance traveled in the peripheral zone of the open-field test (P<0.001), reduced the contents of serum ACTH and CORT (P<0.05, P<0.000 1), and decreased the number of PVN c-Fos-positive cell and the percentage of c-Fos/mCherry double-positive cells among the mCherry-positive cells (P<0.05), while serum CRH presented a lowering trend without statistically significant difference. The ΔF/F area under the curve and peak ΔF/F within the 0-5 s time window were considerably lower during and after EA than EA pre-treatment (P<0.001, P<0.05, P<0.000 1). Under the subthreshold stress, chemogenetic activation of PVN CRH neurons prolonged the immobility time in the forced swimming and tail suspension tests (P<0.000 1, P<0.001) and reduced the distance traveled in the peripheral zone in the open-field test (P<0.05, P<0.001);after EA, these behavioral changes were reversed (P<0.001, P<0.000 1, P<0.05).
EA at LI4 and LR3 can ameliorate CRS-induced depressive-like behaviors by down-regulating hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis-related hormone responses, reducing PVN neuronal activation, decreasing the proportion of c-Fos-positive cells among the mCherry-labeled PVN CRH neurons, and modulating event-related PVN CRH neuron calcium activity.

papers.title: [TH-positive neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla mediating electroacupuncture to improve intestinal motility dysfunction in functional constipated mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Wang D, He Z, Yu M, Wu R, Deng X, Luo Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the role of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) in the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on intestinal dysmotility in mice with functional constipation (FC).
Firstly, transsynaptic tracing virus was employed to identify brain regions projecting to the proximal colon. Secondly, eighteen C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the normal, model, and EA groups, with 6 mice in each group. FC model was established by oral administration of loperamide hydrochloride. Mice in the EA group received EA at "Tianshu" (ST25) and "Shangjuxu" (ST37), 5 days per treatment course for 2 courses. After intervention, the defecation status of mice in each group was observed, and the fecal water content was determined, the time for the first black stool excretion was recorded, the small-intestinal propulsion rate was measured. Serum and colonic TH levels were determined by ELISA. TH/c-Fos co-expression in the RVLM was assessed by immunofluorescence staining. Subsequently, 12 C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into the control virus+clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) group and inhibitory-virus+CNO group, with 6 mice per group. Another 18 C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to the control virus+CNO group, EA group, and excitatory-virus+CNO+EA group, with 6 mice per group. The corresponding viral vectors were injected into the RVLM, followed by intraperitoneal administration of CNO (1 mg/kg) 21 d after viral expression. Mice in the EA and excitatory-virus+CNO+EA groups received EA treatment as described above 30 min after the administration of CNO. Following completion of EA treatment, fecal parameters and intestinal motility were assessed as described above. Finally, rAAV-hSyn-GCaMP6s virus was injected into the RVLM of another 18 C57BL/6J mice. After 21 days of viral transduction, mice were randomly assigned to normal control, model control, and model+EA groups (6 mice per group). Mice in the model+EA group received EA treatment as described above. Post-EA intervention, multichannel fiber photometry was employed to record calcium signal dynamics in RVLM neurons.
Neuronal fibers in the RVLM formed synaptic connections with the proximal colon. Compared with the normal group, the model group exhibited prolonged first black stool expulsion time, reduced total fecal pellet counts, decreased fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01), and elevated TH levels in serum and colon (P<0.01). TH and c-Fos, as well as TH/c-Fos co-expression positive cell counts in the RVLM, were all significantly increased (P<0.001). Compared with the model group, the EA group showed shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01), and reduced TH levels in serum and colon (P<0.01). TH and c-Fos expression, as well as TH/c-Fos positive cell counts in the RVLM, were all significantly decreased (P<0.001). Compared with the control virus+CNO group, the inhibitory-virus+CNO group exhibited shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, and elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the control virus+CNO group, the EA group showed shortened first black stool expulsion time, increased total fecal pellet counts, elevated fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the EA group, the excitatory-virus+CNO+EA group showed prolonged first black stool expulsion time, reduced total fecal pellet counts, and decreased fecal water content and small intestinal transit rate (P<0.001, P<0.01). Compared with the normal control group, the model control group exhibited significantly increased Ca2+ activity in the RVLM (P<0.001), whereas EA significantly reduced RVLM Ca2+ activity compared with the model control group (P<0.001).
EA at ST25 and ST37 may improve intestinal dysmotility in FC mice by suppressing the activity of TH-positive neurons in the RVLM.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 침 치료의 장운동 조절 기전 후보로 RVLM의 TH 양성 뉴런 억제를 제시하지만, 마우스 실험 결과이므로 임상적 일반화에는 주의가 필요하다.

papers.title: [Mechanism of electroacupuncture at "Hegu" (LI4) in regulating the VP-TG pathway for trigeminal neuralgia].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Zhang H, Wang D, Liu Z, Wu Z, Chen Y, Chen N et al.
papers.abstract:
To establish a mouse model of trigeminal neuropathic pain induced by chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (CION), screen the optimal frequency of electroacupuncture (EA) for trigeminal neuralgia (TN), so as to explore the peripheral-central interaction mechanism of the "Hegu" (LI4)-ventral posterior nucleus (VP)-trigeminal ganglion (TG) pathway.
Male C57BL/6J mice were used to establish the TN model via the CION method. EA (2 Hz or 100 Hz or 2 Hz/100 Hz) was applied to bilateral LI4 for 30 min each time, once every other day, for a total of 12 times. Mechanical withdrawal thresholds (MWTs) of the vibrissal pad were measured using von Frey filaments. Anxiety-like behaviors were assessed by the elevated plus maze (EPM) test, and depression-like behaviors by the tail suspension (TS) test and sucrose preference (SP) test. Neuronal activities in 8 brain regions, including the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN), VP, and spinal trigeminal nucleus caudalis (Sp5C), etc. were evaluated by c-Fos immunofluorescence. Double immunofluorescence labeling was used to detect co-expressions of c-Fos with 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), glutamate (Glu), or γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the DRN to identify activated neuron subtypes. Neural connectivities between "Hegu"-dorsal root ganglion (DRG)-spinal dorsal horn (DH)- VP and TG-Sp5C-VP were traced using chemical or viral tracers.
After the treatment, compared with the sham group, the MWTs of mice were significantly decreased in the model group (P<0.000 1). The MWTs in the 2 Hz, 100 Hz, and 2 Hz/100 Hz EA groups were all increased (P<0.05, P<0.001), and the analgesic effect of the 2 Hz/100 Hz EA was superior to those of the 2 Hz and 100 Hz EA groups (P<0.05, P<0.01). In the EPM test, the time spent in the open arms was significantly decreased in the model group (P<0.000 1), while it was increased in the 100 Hz EA and 2 Hz/100 Hz EA groups (P<0.01, P<0.000 1). Moreover, the time spent in the open arms was longer in the 2 Hz/100 Hz EA group than in the 2 Hz EA group (P<0.01). In the TS and SP tests, the immobility time was increased and the sucrose preference was decreased in the model group (P<0.000 1), whereas EA reversed these changes (P<0.000 1, P<0.001). The 2 Hz/100 Hz EA group showed a more significant improvement in depression-like behavior than the 2 Hz and 100 Hz EA groups (P<0.05, P<0.01). Tracing results showed that after injection of a chemical tracer into LI4, tracer signals were observed in the C6 and C7 DRGs. After injection of a retrograde trans-multisynaptic virus into the VP, viral expression was observed in the DH, Sp5C, and TG. Immunofluorescence results showed that neuronal activity in the Sp5C, VP, ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM), parafascicular nucleus (PaF), and DRN was increased in the model group (P<0.01, P<0.000 1, P<0.05), while EA reversed these changes (P<0.000 1, P<0.01, P<0.001). Compared with the sham group, the model group showed decreased 5-HT neuronal activity (P<0.000 1) and increased Glu and GABA neuronal activities (P<0.000 1, P<0.05) in the DRN, all of which were reversed by 2 Hz/100 Hz EA (P<0.001, P<0.000 1, P<0.05).
The 2 Hz/100 Hz EA is superior to single-frequency stimulation in improving mechanical hypersensitivity and associated negative affective behaviors in CION model mice. Under CION conditions, abnormal activation was observed in the Sp5C, VP, VPM, PaF, and DRN, accompanied by decreased activity of 5-HT neurons and increased activities of GABA and Glu neurons in the DRN, and 2 Hz/100 Hz EA can reverse these phenomena. The tracing results indicated the existence of neuroanatomical connections of the LI4-DRG-DH-VP and TG-Sp5C-VP pathways. These findings provide objective evidence for investigating the LI4-VP-TG response mechanism underlying EA intervention in TN.

papers.title: [Comparative study on intervention effects of electroacupuncture at single point "Zusanli" (ST36), "Sanyinjiao" (SP6) and combined points on irritable bowel syndrome mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Qian S, Zhang L, Zhang J, Cui G, Huang T
papers.abstract:
To compare the differences in interventional effects among three stimulation modalities:electroacupuncture (EA) at single acupoint "Zusanli" (ST36), single acupoint "Sanyinjiao" (SP6), and their combination (ST36 + SP6), on behavioral and histological outcomes in a mouse model of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and to examine the differential neuronal responses in the peripheral and central nervous systems under these modalities, so as to provide experimental evidence for exploring the neural mechanisms underlying acupoint combination stimulation in IBS treatment.
An IBS model was established in male C57BL/6J mice by intrarectal instillation of zymosan. The mice were randomly divided into blank control group, model group, ST36 group, SP6 group, and acupoint combination group (n=20 per group except n=18 for the model group). After 7 consecutive days of EA stimulation (2 Hz/100 Hz, 1 mA, 15 min per session, once daily), abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia (referred pain) was assessed using von Frey filaments, motor function by rotarod test, and 3D spontaneous fine behavioral characteristics by an AI-based unsupervised 3D behavioral analysis system. Colon tissue structure and inflammatory levels were observed by HE staining, and colonic inflammatory cytokine expressions were detected by Western blot, to evaluate the symptom-relieving effects of single versus combined acupoint stimulation. For neural tracing, retrograde viral tracers were injected into ST36 and SP6 to label dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons innervating these acupoints in C57BL/6J mice. In vivo two-photon calcium imaging was performed to record DRG neuronal responses to different EA modalities (1 mA, 1 min) in Thy1-GCaMP6s mice, and activity-dependent neuronal labeling was applied using transgenic TRAP2;Ai14 mice to identify central neurons activated by EA (2 Hz/100 Hz, 1 mA, 15 min per session), aiming to reveal peripheral-central neuronal response differences between single and combined acupoint stimulation.
Compared with the blank control group, the model group showed increased abdominal mechanical withdrawal frequency and area under the curve (P<0.001, P<0.05), decreased motor function (latency to fall and rotarod speed at fall, P<0.01), aggravated colonic tissue damage and inflammatory responses (P<0.001), elevated expressions of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α, P<0.001), and altered spontaneous behavioral patterns (P<0.001, P<0.01, P<0.05). All three EA modalities significantly alleviated abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia in IBS mice (P<0.001, P<0.05, P<0.01), with the combined stimulation showing a larger effective interventional window than either single acupoint. Compared with single-acupoint stimulation, combined stimulation also more effectively restored colonic tissue damage, reduced TNF-α expression (P<0.05), and shortened the duration of spontaneous arching episodes and altered the transition patterns among different spontaneous behavioral actions (P<0.01, P<0.05). DRG neurons exhibited highly heterogeneous responses to the three stimulation modalities, which could be classified into 3 major categories and 7 subcategories based on their firing characteristics. Furthermore, combined stimulation activated a greater number of DRG neurons than single acupoint stimulation (P<0.05), and the neuronal calcium signal intensity was also higher (P<0.05). Finally, significant differences were observed in the number of responsive neurons across different brain regions under the three modalities. The activated neuronal populations evoked by ST36, SP6, and combined stimulation showed maximal overlap in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN), whereas the overlap was minimal in the insular cortex (IC), suggesting that IC neuronal activation requires the synergistic effect of combined acupoint stimulation.
Combined stimulation at ST36 and SP6 produces superior therapeutic effects over single acupoint stimulation in ameliorating abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia, colonic structural damage, inflammatory status, and spontaneous behavioral changes induced by visceral pain in IBS model mice, and this advantage may arise from the synergistic integration of peripheral and central neuronal responses to different EA signals.

papers.title: [The body-brain mechanism of acupuncture: insight and inspiration from neuroimmunology and regulation of organ function].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Gao X
papers.abstract: Acupuncture, as a typical representative of non-drug therapy, regulates central functions by activating the peripheral nervous system, and has become a leading hotspot in the field of neuromodulation. Focusing on the body-brain mechanism of acupuncture effects, this article systematically reviews the cutting-edge interdisciplinary advancements in acupuncture research and modern life sciences from 3 dimensions: neuro-immune anti-inflammatory actions, target organ function regulation, and "one acupoint affecting multiple organs" intervention for comorbidities. To analyze the key issues, clarify academic viewpoints, and trigger inspirations and discussions, the following are the main points: 1) Based on the established understanding that acupuncture stimulation activates autonomic nerve pathways such as the brainstem vagus-adrenal and spinal cord sympathetic-splenic axes, to exert anti-inflammatory effects, it has also been revealed that some vagus nerves can directly traverse and form synaptic connections with catecholaminergic neurons in the celiac ganglion via collateral branches, rather than relay on postsynaptic neurons. It further seeks to clarify the hierarchical relationship among the catecholamine anti-inflammatory, cholinergic anti-inflammatory, sympathetic/parasympathetic nerve pathways, particularly paying attention to the relationship between the concentration-dependent receptor affinity of norepinephrine in the inflammatory microenvironment and its association with acupuncture effects. 2) Current researches have demonstrated that acupuncture regulates the homeostasis of the body and internal organs by rebalancing the sympathetic-parasympathetic system at multiple levels, identifying the "off-target" phenomenon caused by the loss of response of tissue cells and receptors under pathological conditions is a key factor affecting the "last mile" of the acupuncture effect. 3) Taking the convergence of different visceral input signaling mediated by the intrinsic structures of the spinal cord, as well as the occurrence of comorbidity in the interactive sensitization of the pelvic and sacral organs as an example, results of modern research have provided possible explanations for the cross-segment's and same-segment's "one acupoint affecting multiple organs" and "multiple acupoints affecting one organ" effects of acupuncture. In summary, this article aims to clarify how acupuncture regulates the body's homeostasis through different body-brain autonomic nervous pathways and levels, and offers a review of existing research through 4 dimensions of thinking and inspiration to stimulate new insights and foster exchange of opinions.

papers.title: Amelioration of early pathological changes in the 3xTg-AD mouse model: Mechanism of action of the Chinese herbal formula Tianqi Granules.
papers.authors: Zhang T, Xu L, Huang W, Chen Z, Miao J, Zhang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline. This study investigated the effects of the Chinese herbal formula Tianqi Granules on early pathological progression in the 3xTg-AD mouse models and investigated the underlying mechanisms. After 31 days of Tianqi Granule treatment initiated at 5 months of age, Tianqi Granules-treated mice showed improved performance in the open-field test, novel object recognition test, and Morris water maze test. Amyloid deposition and glial activation were attenuated, and immunoreactivity for interleukin-1β and LC3 was reduced. Hippocampal transcriptome sequencing at multiple time points showed that, in untreated mice, early pathological progression occurred in three successive phases, with the dominant processes shifting from compensatory programs to failing homeostasis and subsequently to degenerative changes. Tianqi Granule treatment was associated with a three-phase response centered on the restoration of homeostasis and involving proteostasis, nuclear processes, lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, and redox-related pathways. Multiple biological domains were engaged rather than a single target. In males, an interferon-related program associated with Irf7 was induced early and shifted in the opposite direction under Tianqi Granule treatment during the same time window. Network pharmacology identified OPRK1 as the only candidate target shared by both sexes, making it a potential target for future investigation. These findings suggest that Tianqi Granule modulates the pathology of Alzheimer's disease through coordinated actions on multiple targets and may influence systemic metabolic homeostasis, providing experimental support for early therapeutic intervention in Alzheimer's disease.

summary.methods: 5개월령부터 31일간 천기과립을 투여한 3xTg-AD 마우스에서 행동검사와 조직학, 면역염색, 히포캠퍼스 전사체 분석 및 네트워크 약리학을 시행한 전임상 연구이다.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 결과는 천기과립이 알츠하이머병 초기 병리의 다중 경로를 조절할 가능성을 시사하지만, 근거는 동물 실험에 기반하므로 임상 적용은 추가 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 마우스 전임상 연구이며 사람 대상 효능과 안전성을 직접 보여주지 못하고, 기전 해석도 탐색적이다.

papers.title: Schaftoside from galgeuntang as a multi-target class I histone deacetylase inhibitor: Integrated molecular docking, dynamics, and systems pharmacology analysis.
papers.authors: Shah FH, Cho JS, Lee SH, Jo YR, Huh SJ, Chung HJ et al.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are enzymes that remove acetyl groups from lysine residues of histone proteins, playing a critical role in gene expression regulation. Particularly, Class I HDACs (HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8) are implicated in cancer development and have attracted significant interest as therapeutic targets. However, developing isoform-selective HDAC inhibitors remains challenging. We screened 1625 phytocompounds from the Korean herbal formulation Galgeuntang using the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology database. After applying drug-likeness filtering, 235 compounds underwent molecular docking against HDAC1, HDAC2, and HDAC8. Schaftoside emerged as the sole candidate engaging all three isoforms, with binding energies of -115.1, -103.8, and -135.5 kcal/mol, respectively. ADMET profiling, quantitative cytotoxicity predictions across multiple cancer cell lines, and in silico gene expression analysis were then performed. One hundred nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable complex formation and PCA-based free energy landscape analysis revealed well-defined conformational minima for each complex. Schaftoside exhibited potent predicted cytotoxicity against hematological and gastrointestinal malignancies (selectivity Index: 8.7-18.6), including the cisplatin-resistant A2780cisR ovarian carcinoma line. In silico transcriptomic profiling predicted downregulation of oncogenic drivers (MYC, STAT3, AKT1) with concurrent upregulation of tumor suppressors (TP53, CDKN1A) and suppression of the HDAC machinery itself. ADMET profiling revealed high aqueous solubility but limited membrane permeability, indicating that structural optimization will be required. Schaftoside therefore constitutes a promising multi-target Class I HDAC inhibitor scaffold, warranting experimental validation through enzymatic assays, histone acetylation analysis, and cell-based cytotoxicity testing.

summary.question: 갈근탕 성분 중 schaftoside가 class I HDAC를 다중 표적으로 억제할 가능성이 있는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: TCMSP 데이터베이스로 갈근탕 유래 1625개 식물성 화합물을 선별한 뒤 도킹, ADMET 예측, in silico 유전자 발현 분석과 100 ns 분자동역학 시뮬레이션을 수행했다.
summary.results: Schaftoside가 HDAC1, HDAC2, HDAC8 모두와 가장 강하게 결합하는 후보로 나타났고, 시뮬레이션에서도 안정적인 복합체 형성이 예측되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 갈근탕 유래 schaftoside는 실험적 검증이 필요한 유망한 class I HDAC 억제제 후보 스캐폴드로 해석할 수 있다.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Pharmacology Identifies IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG as Candidate Targets of Cortex Dictamni in Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Feng R, Liu X, Wei J, Ma T
papers.abstract: Cortex Dictamni has been used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for inflammatory skin disorders, but its potential molecular targets in atopic dermatitis (AD) remain incompletely characterized. Active compounds and predicted targets of Cortex Dictamni were retrieved from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform and integrated with bulk-transcriptomic differential-expression data and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Protein-protein interaction, functional-enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA)-based immune-cell and pathway analyses were performed with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. Molecular docking was used to predict luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2 binding poses, and candidate-gene expression was assessed in TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT keratinocytes treated with low concentrations of purified dictamnine. Eighteen active components yielded 170 predicted targets; 88 overlapped with AD-related genes, and 43 of these were differentially expressed. Intersecting 366 cell-type-specific differentially expressed genes with 42 targets identified IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG. IRF1, PTGS2, and TNF were upregulated in specific immune-cell populations, whereas IFNG was downregulated in natural killer cells. Ribosome-pathway enrichment was observed across five immune-cell types. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, immune-signature correlations were gene-specific and bidirectional, whereas Hallmark-pathway correlations were nonsignificant. Docking predicted possible binding poses for luteolin-IFNG and β-sitosterol-PTGS2. In TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT cells, 6.25 and 12.5 µM dictamnine reduced all four mRNAs, whereas 12.5 µM dictamnine alone had no significant effect. Collectively, IRF1, PTGS2, TNF, and IFNG were nominated as potential Cortex Dictamni-associated targets in AD, and low-dose purified dictamnine provided preliminary mRNA-level support. These findings do not establish crude-herb efficacy or direct target-compound interactions and require protein-level, mechanistic, in vivo, and clinical validation.

papers.title: Progress on the Anti-inflammatory Mechanisms of Moxibustion in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
papers.authors: Xu M, Nie H, Li L, Ai J, Chen W, Xu C et al.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, is driven by persistent airway inflammation involving complex pathways. Despite advances in conventional therapies, challenges remain in the effective control of steroid-resistant inflammation and systemic complications. Moxibustion is a traditional Chinese therapy that has shown promise in alleviating COPD-related inflammation by targeting these pathways. Clinical studies have suggested that moxibustion can regulate inflammatory cells (macrophages, neutrophils, Th17 cells, and regulatory T [Treg] cells) and mediators (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8), and these mechanisms correlate with improved lung function, reduced exacerbations, and enhanced immune balance. However, current evidence is limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous methodologies, and a lack of high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs), resulting in an unclear independent therapeutic efficacy of moxibustion for COPD. While preliminary findings highlight its potential as an adjunct therapy, rigorous multicenter RCTs are imperative with large sample sizes and standardized protocols to validate its anti-inflammatory efficacy, elucidate dose-response relationships, and comprehensively evaluate safety profiles. This review aims to integrate traditional medical theory with modern immune inflammation biology, and summarize progress on the mechanism of inflammation regulation of moxibustion in the treatment of COPD. It mainly puts forward the view that moxibustion may treat COPD through TLR4/NF-κB pathway and IL-33/ST2 pathway, and points out the limitations of the existing related research. It emphasizes the need for more direct mechanism explanation and clinical research to verify.

papers.title: Multi-Target Mechanism of Corydalis yanhusuo Against Fibromyalgia Syndrome: A Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking Study.
papers.authors: Zhou T, Liang X
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) is a chronic pain disorder with limited therapeutic options. This study aimed to predict the multi-target mechanism of Corydalis yanhusuo against FMS using network pharmacology and molecular docking. Active ingredients were retrieved from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform (TCMSP) with oral bioavailability (OB) ≥30% and drug-likeness (DL) ≥0.18. Disease targets were obtained from GeneCards. Overlapping targets were used for protein-protein interaction (PPI), Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses. Molecular docking was performed using CB-Dock2. A total of 49 active ingredients and 53 overlapping targets were identified. Hub targets included tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-6 (IL6), interleukin-1 beta (IL1B), estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1), and prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2). KEGG analysis revealed interleukin-17 (IL-17), TNF, nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction pathways. Predicted docking scores ranged from -10.1 to -6.5 kcal/mol, with stigmasterol showing the lowest predicted binding energy to cholinergic receptor muscarinic 3 (CHRM3) (-10.1 kcal/mol). These findings suggest that C. yanhusuo may exert potential anti-FMS effects through multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway mechanisms, particularly by modulating neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter signaling. Experimental validation is required.

papers.title: Gut-Brain Axis and Appetite: A Hypothesis-Generating Narrative Review of Traditional Chinese Medicine for Non-Organic Poor Appetite in Children.
papers.authors: Qiao J, Zhang H
papers.abstract: Non-organic poor appetite/feeding difficulty in children is characterized by persistent poor appetite or reduced food intake without the body-image disturbance or fear of weight gain characteristic of anorexia nervosa. This hypothesis-generating narrative review examines gut-brain axis dysfunction in this condition and evaluates proposed mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) interventions. Peer-reviewed literature published from January 2000 to August 2026 was reviewed using PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI). Human, animal, and review studies relevant to appetite regulation, pathogenesis, or TCM were considered, while studies exclusively concerning anorexia nervosa were excluded unless used as clearly identified indirect mechanistic evidence. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), where applicable. The evidence was organized across four dimensions: central appetite-regulatory networks, including neurotransmitters; brain-gut peptides; intestinal barrier function; and gut microbiota. Available studies suggest alterations across these dimensions and propose that specific TCM interventions, including herbal formulas, acupuncture, and tuina, may influence related pathways. Evidence concerning microbiota composition and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) is primarily preclinical or indirect, and functional restoration of gut-brain communication has not been demonstrated in affected children. Overall, the evidence is heterogeneous, predominantly correlational, and frequently derived from animal models, in-vitro studies, other disease populations, or specific interventions. Direct pediatric mechanistic evidence remains limited, causal pathways have not been established, and no efficacy conclusion can currently be drawn.

papers.title: Beyond non-adherence: qualitative insights into how patients strategically navigate pluralistic chronic care in West Africa.
papers.authors: Abdul-Samed AB, Mamadou OT, Kabore AT, Amarteyfio KNAA, Yamba SAK, Diarra A et al.
papers.abstract:
Across West Africa, people living with chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) routinely seek care across biomedical, traditional and spiritual sectors. Patients often navigate these pluralistic health systems intentionally, responding to economic and social constraints, yet movement away from biomedical care is commonly interpreted as non-adherence. We examine how and why patients in West Africa negotiate their NCD care pathways across multiple sectors, and how they exercise agency within these constraints.
We used a multiple qualitative case design, drawing on data from 11 purposively selected municipalities and districts in Burkina Faso, Ghana and Niger. Semistructured interviews were conducted with 84 participants: people with hypertension, diabetes or common mental health conditions (n=29); biomedical providers (n=29); traditional and spiritual healers (n=13); caregivers (n=3) and policy makers (n=10). Interviews in English, French and five local languages were analysed thematically, guided by frameworks on healthcare pluralism, patient agency and care-seeking trajectories.
Three patterns of therapeutic navigation emerged across all three countries, shaped by collective decision-making within extended family and peer networks, economic constraints and expectations of cure. First, when biomedical costs became untenable, patients shifted from biomedicine to traditional providers, carrying their diagnoses into the folk sector and often returning to biomedical care when resources allowed. Second, some patients concurrently maintained biomedical treatment while running self-managed traditional regimens, assigning distinct functions to each sector: biomedicine for diagnosis and monitoring, traditional medicine for the prospect of cure. Third, for mental health, families followed a spiritual-first trajectory from the outset, driven by explanatory models of spiritual causation rather than service availability or cost. Across all three patterns, patients frequently concealed their pluralistic practices from biomedical providers, fearing reprimand or finding no clinical space in which to disclose.
Pluralistic care-seeking is a form of deliberate, conditioned agency, not simple non-adherence. Improving chronic NCD care requires more sustainably affordable biomedical services, consultation environments that enable open disclosure of pluralistic practice without penalty and health indicators that capture therapeutic navigation rather than biomedical endpoints alone.

papers.title: Spontaneous Resorption of Prolapsed Lumbar Disc Herniation Facilitated by Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Tao L, Zhang S, Cheng M, Zhang B, Lai F
papers.abstract:
While conservative management often improves lumbar disc herniation (LDH) symptoms and promotes spontaneous resorption over time, the clinical value of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) in accelerating this process remains underexplored.
We present a 36-year-old female with an acute, massive right-sided L5/S1 disc prolapse. Following a staged conservative regimen and the subsequent introduction of ESWT combined with acupuncture. Lastly her radicular pain and numbness almost completely resolved.
Staged conservative intervention is highly effective for prolapsed LDH. The timely application of ESWT provides a novel, non-invasive strategy that promotes neovascularization and immune phagocytosis, strongly supporting the conservative management of massive disc herniations.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological traditional Chinese medicine interventions for depression: bibliometric mapping of Chinese databases and WoSCC, 2000-2025.
papers.authors: Dong S, Lian Y, Xie J, Cao S, Yang J, Qi F et al.
papers.abstract:
The aim of the study was to characterize publication activity, collaboration structures, keyword themes, and temporal changes in the literature on non-pharmacological traditional Chinese medicine interventions for depression.
Journal records published from 2000 to 2025 were obtained from CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Eligibility combined mechanical rules with independent paired assessment of 2,089 boundary records and reference-based reconciliation. The final corpora contained 5,385 Chinese and 721 WoSCC records. Full-counting collaboration and keyword networks were analyzed using weighted Louvain communities, cosine-distance silhouettes, two-state burst intervals, and resolution, seed, Leiden, and terminology sensitivity analyses. Selected graph quantities were cross-checked in R/igraph. Additional checks evaluated record-identity consistency, linkage sensitivity, and annual keyword availability denominators.
Chinese output peaked at 390 records in 2021, while WoSCC output reached 118 records in 2025. Complete author networks contained 12,141 Chinese and 2,933 WoSCC nodes and were sparse (densities 0.000410 and 0.003572). Eligible keyword networks contained 569 Chinese and 81 WoSCC terms. Weighted Louvain yielded five Chinese communities (Q = 0.194124; mean silhouette = 0.005173) and four WoSCC communities (Q = 0.134767; mean silhouette = 0.029369). Stability analyses showed only moderate agreement across seeds and alternative algorithms, indicating that the communities are exploratory summaries rather than discrete topic classes. Keyword availability denominators materially altered some WoSCC community time profiles.
The literature expanded substantially and centered on acupuncture-related interventions, poststroke depression, evidence synthesis terminology, exercise-based techniques, sleep, and experimental themes. Sparse collaboration networks and overlapping thematic interpretations indicate opportunities for broader collaboration and more consistent terminology. Bibliometric prominence does not establish efficacy, safety, mechanism, or causality.

papers.title: Jianpi Huazhuo Formula Suppresses Choroidal Neovascularization by Modulating the AKT1/MAPK3/IL6 Axis.
papers.authors: Yang L, Zhang S, Han C
papers.abstract: This study elucidates the therapeutic mechanisms of Jianpi Huazhuo formula (JHF) in suppressing laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV) through the modulation of the AKT1/MAPK3/IL6 signaling pathway. Utilizing a murine CNV model, JHF administration markedly attenuated vascular leakage, as evidenced by fluorescein angiography, optical coherence tomography, and fundus imaging. Integrated network pharmacology pinpointed AKT1, MAPK3, and IL6 as pivotal targets, with functional enrichment analyses highlighting their roles in key processes such as reactive oxygen species response and inflammatory regulation, particularly within the PI3K-Akt and IL-17 pathways. Molecular docking validated robust interactions between JHF-derived compounds (e.g., luteolin and quercetin) and these targets, exhibiting binding energies ranging from -4.0 to -7.41 kcal/mol. Subsequent molecular assays confirmed that JHF significantly reduced AKT1, MAPK3, and IL6 expression at transcriptional and translational levels in RPE-choroid tissues. Time-dependent expression profiling further revealed sustained suppression of these targets throughout CNV progression, and in vitro validation in an oxidative stress-induced ARPE-19 cell model confirmed the direct regulatory effect of JHF on this signaling axis. These findings demonstrate that JHF exerts its antiangiogenic effects via a multitarget network centered on the AKT1/MAPK3/IL6 axis. The study innovatively delineates JHF's polypharmacological mode of action, offering novel insights for leveraging traditional Chinese medicine in managing neovascular ocular diseases.

papers.title: Structural characterization and structure-activity relationship of polysaccharides from Curcuma kwangsiensis extracted sequentially: Anti-Alzheimer's activity in an AlCl3-induced zebrafish model.
papers.authors: Fan X, Li J, Ma M, Li R, Jiang J, Yang L et al.
papers.abstract: Research on polysaccharides from Curcuma kwangsiensis has primarily focused on hot-water extraction, while mechanistic investigations and structure-activity relationship (SAR) analyses remain scarce. Here, four polysaccharides (GYJ-W, GYJ-C, GYJ-Na, and GYJ-0.1 M) were obtained employing water, 0.05 M CDTA, 0.05 M Na2CO3, and 0.1 M NaOH. Their physicochemical properties and in vivo efficacy against-AD were evaluated to elucidate the SAR. Results showed that the extraction methods significantly affected GYJPs' yields (0.52-4.49%), monosaccharide compositions, molecular weight (3.06 × 104-2.29 × 105 Da), and anti-AD activities. Carbohydrate content ranged from 47.12% to 55.67%, with protein and uronic acid at 3.00%-15.58% and 3.06%-6.45%, respectively. Glucose predominated (23.97%-97.16%); GYJ-Na contained the highest fucose (48.89%) and glucuronic acid (11.58%). Despite significant composition and Mw variations, Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) and thermal stability analyses confirmed that the core structural features of GYJPs were largely preserved. In vivo anti-AD activity assays indicated that GYJPs effectively alleviated locomotion impairments and reduced neuronal apoptosis. Mechanistically, the GYJPs restored cholinergic function, suppressed appb and mapta expression, inhibited neuroinflammation (il-6, il-1β, tnf-α), and enhanced antioxidant capacity (gstp and sod1). Correlation analysis revealed that Mw and monosaccharide composition are the two key determinants underlying the anti-AD bioactivity of GYJPs. Overall, these findings highlight GYJPs as promising multi-target AD drug candidates and support rational utilization of traditional Chinese medicine resources.

papers.title: The clinical efficacy of acupuncture therapy in patients with sudden sensorineural hearing loss: a systematic review, meta-analysis and network meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Zhong W, Zeng Z, Li X, Luo Y, Zhang B
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture has gained increasing attention for the treatment of sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL). Hence, it is necessary to systematically evaluate and rank the effectiveness of acupuncture therapies for SSNHL.
A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, SinoMed, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang databases from inception to January 1, 2026. Risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and 95% conﬁdence intervals (CI) were used to estimate the eﬀect using R 4.4.1.
A total of 36 studies involving 3360 patients diagnosed with SSNHL were included. Acupuncture combined with guideline treatment, especially glucocorticoids, could improve the overall effective rate (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.15 to 1.23, I2 = 11.1%, 95% CI: 0.0% to 42.8%, p < 0.0001, k = 36), with most trials reporting consistent enhancements in pure-tone audiometry. Among them, extra acupuncture emerged as the preferred adjunct, with routine acupuncture next, while moxibustion may serve as an alternative to either. A three-week course is currently recommended, and extending beyond that is unlikely to yield further meaningful efficacy. However, based on current findings, point injection may not be recommend for SSNHL. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy, currently used as a salvage therapy, may overlap with the complementary effects of acupuncture, and evidence to distinguish their efficacy remains limited.
Certain acupuncture therapies may be a complementary or alternative treatment for SSNHL, though the certainty of evidence rating by the CINeMA is too low to permit more than a tentative interpretation.

papers.title: In vitro anthelmintic activity of the monoterpene linalool, alone and combined with the nematophagous fungus Duddingtonia flagrans, in the control of gastrointestinal nematodes in horses.
papers.authors: Lima APG, Amorim ACD, Lima AMS, Batista SP, Alvares FBV, Feitosa TF et al.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated, in vitro, the anthelmintic activity of the monoterpene linalool, alone and in association with the fungus Duddingtonia flagrans, against gastrointestinal nematodes of horses. Nematodes from the superfamily Strongyloidea, obtained from naturally infected horses, were used. The ovicidal activity of linalool was evaluated using the Egg Hatch Test (EHT). The larvicidal activity was evaluated using the Larval Motility Inhibition Test (LMIT), in which infective larvae (L3) were assigned to experimental groups treated with linalool alone (0.15, 0.3, 0.6, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, and 80 mg/mL), D. flagrans conidia alone (100,000, 500,000, and 1,000,000 conidia), or the combination of both. In the EHT, linalool completely inhibited egg hatching (100%) at all concentrations of 0.25 mg/mL and above, with an LC₅₀ of 0.15 mg/mL (0.015%). In the LMIT, linalool completely inhibited larval motility (100%) at all concentrations of 0.5 mg/mL and above, with an LC₅₀ of 0.103 mg/mL (0.010%). The association with the fungus D. flagrans promoted a significant reduction (p ≤ 0.05) in the number of live larvae after 72 h, reaching 100% inhibition within 14 days. The groups treated only with conidia showed lower efficacy, whereas the association with linalool enhanced the antiparasitic effect without impairing trap formation or the predatory capacity of the fungus. Thus, the results demonstrated that linalool has relevant ovicidal and larvicidal activity, and that its association with D. flagrans constitutes a promising alternative for the biological control of helminth infections in horses.

papers.title: Gene expression, MMGBSA, molecular and induced-fit docking of Bambusa vulgaris phytocompounds in endoplasmic reticulum stress induced by streptozotocin.
papers.authors: Aladenika YV, Akinjiyan MO, Ojo FM, Tanimowo OB, Elekofehinti OO, Adanlawo IG
papers.abstract:
Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) has been linked to insulin resistance and diabetes mellitus. Bambusa vulgaris, a tropical bamboo species widely used in traditional medicine, is used to reduce oxidative stress and as an antidiabetic agent. This study investigates the effect of B. vulgaris on ERS-related gene expression and conducts a computational analysis of B. vulgaris phytocompounds.
ERS was induced intraperitoneally by 60 mg/kg streptozotocin (STZ) dissolved in citrate buffer. Thirty experimental rats (n = 5) were divided into six groups: control, ERS control, metformin (100 mg/kg), and B. vulgaris aqueous extract (BV) orally administered groups (50, 100, and 200 mg/kg). Fasting blood glucose was monitored with a glucometer; RT-PCR was used for gene expression after 21 days of treatment. Molecular and induced-fit docking, free binding energy, and ADMET profiling of B. vulgaris compounds with PERK were evaluated using Schrödinger.
GRP78, CHOP, ATF4, and PERK mRNA expressions were markedly (p < 0.05) upregulated relative to the control upon induction with STZ after 72 h. BV (50 and 100 mg/kg) significantly downregulated these genes' expression compared with untreated ERS rats. Luteolin and chlorogenic acid had the lowest docking scores (-10.764 kcal/mol and - 10.725 kcal/mol), with strong induced-fit scores and free binding energies (-42.2 kcal/mol and - 39.33 kcal/mol, respectively). Both comply with Lipinski's rules of drug-likeness. Isovitexin has the lowest free binding energy - 50.91 kcal/mol.
This work suggests that BV and its compounds downregulate genes associated with ERS and promote normoglycemia.
