papers.title: Advances in assessment systems and non-pharmacological intervention strategies for cancer-related fatigue following transarterial chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma: a narrative review.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Yang S, Yao X, Ren Y, Ding T, Gao J, Shentu L
papers.abstract:
Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a primary treatment for intermediate to advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a prevalent and distressing symptom following TACE that significantly impairs patients' recovery and health-related quality of life. This review aimed to systematically summarize the current evidence on CRF screening, assessment, and non-pharmacological interventions specifically tailored to the post-TACE HCC population, and to propose an integrated, nurse-led clinical management framework.
A narrative review was conducted by systematically searching PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI for literature published up to April 2026. The search encompassed peer-reviewed original research articles (including randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, cross-sectional studies, and meta-analyses), clinical practice guidelines, and expert consensus reports. The level of evidence for each intervention category was evaluated using the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (OCEBM) grading system. The literature search focused on CRF epidemiology, pathophysiology, validated assessment tools, non-pharmacological interventions (including exercise, psychosocial support, nutritional management, and traditional Chinese medicine therapies), and nursing management models in HCC patients following TACE.
CRF following TACE is a multifactorial symptom driven by treatment-induced inflammation, hepatic dysfunction, and psychological distress. Validated screening tools, including the Brief Fatigue Inventory (BFI), Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS), and EORTC QLQ-C30 fatigue subscale, are recommended for routine use, though to the best of our knowledge, no CRF assessment tool developed specifically for the post-TACE HCC population has been validated to date. A structured screening pathway encompassing baseline assessment, perioperative monitoring, and long-term follow-up was identified as essential for early detection. Among non-pharmacological interventions, individualized exercise prescriptions (aerobic and resistance training) have been most consistently supported across randomised trials and meta-analyses for alleviating CRF, followed by cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and nutritional support. Traditional Chinese medicine approaches, including acupoint massage, auricular acupressure, and moxibustion, showed preliminary potential but require further high-quality validation. A nurse-led multidisciplinary care model integrating assessment, individualized intervention planning, and continuous coordination has been proposed as a promising operational framework for CRF management, endorsed by international CRF practice frameworks.
Effective management of CRF after TACE requires a comprehensive, evidence-based approach spanning standardized screening, multimodal non-pharmacological interventions, and a nurse-coordinated multidisciplinary care model. Integrating routine CRF assessment into standard TACE clinical pathways and developing TACE-specific assessment tools are priorities for future research and clinical practice.

papers.title: Pharmacological basis of Suhexiang Wan in ischemic stroke: identification and functional characterization of piperlongumine as a brain-distributed bioactive constituent associated with STAT3-mediated blood-brain barrier protection.
papers.authors: Wang J, Ma S, Yu D, Wang Y, Ma C, Ma D et al.
papers.abstract:
Suhexiang Wan (SHXW) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula that has been traditionally used for stroke-related disorders, including sudden loss of consciousness, neurological dysfunction, and hemiplegia. Although modern pharmacological studies have suggested its neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties, the brain-distributed constituents potentially associated with its therapeutic effects in ischemic stroke (IS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to elucidate the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by identifying brain-distributed constituents and investigating a candidate constituent potentially associated with its protective effects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI), with particular emphasis on blood-brain barrier (BBB) protection.
SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue under middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) conditions were characterized using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Integrated network pharmacology analysis was performed to predict potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Piperlongumine (PIP) was further confirmed and quantified in SHXW and brain tissue using an authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS approach. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, biophysical binding assays, and cellular target-engagement experiments were used to investigate the interaction between PIP and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). The protective effects and associated mechanisms were evaluated in a mouse MCAO/R model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-induced brain microvascular endothelial cell injury model.
Among 1,991 putatively annotated constituents of SHXW, 55 SHXW-derived constituents were detected in brain tissue under MCAO/R conditions. In the MCAO/R mouse model, SHXW significantly improved neurological deficits, reduced infarct volume and brain edema, decreased BBB permeability, and restored tight junction protein expression. Among the brain-detected constituents, PIP, a natural alkaloid derived from Piper longum L., was selected for further investigation based on its detection in brain tissue, network topology characteristics, predicted association with STAT3, and reported pharmacological relevance to ischemic injury. Authentic standard-based LC-MS/MS confirmed PIP in SHXW and brain tissue, with a PIP content of 48.21 ± 1.10 μg/g in SHXW and a brain concentration of 159.67 ± 8.37 ng/g at 2 h after SHXW administration. Biophysical and cellular target-engagement assays supported the interaction between PIP and STAT3. PIP partially recapitulated the protective effects of SHXW by alleviating neurological deficits, preserving BBB integrity, restoring endothelial barrier function, and suppressing STAT3-associated inflammatory responses. STAT3 knockdown partially phenocopied the endothelial protective effects of PIP, whereas restoration of STAT3 expression in STAT3-knockdown cells reversed the protective phenotype. PIP treatment attenuated the injury-associated changes following STAT3 restoration, supporting the functional involvement of STAT3-associated signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection.
This study provides new insights into the pharmacological basis of SHXW in IS by integrating chemical profiling, brain distribution analysis, and pharmacological validation. SHXW exerted protective effects against CIRI and preserved BBB integrity. Among the SHXW-derived constituents detected in brain tissue, PIP was identified and functionally characterized as a bioactive candidate associated with BBB protection. The findings support the involvement of PIP-STAT3 interaction and STAT3-associated inflammatory signaling in PIP-mediated BBB protection. These results provide pharmacological evidence linking the traditional application of SHXW with its modern molecular mechanisms while highlighting brain-distribution-guided approaches for investigating the therapeutic basis of complex TCM formulas.

papers.title: Schisandrin B attenuates the platelet activation-thrombosis cascade through inhibition of Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/AKT and Extracellular signal-regulated kinase-Talin-mediated integrin αIIbβ3 signaling.
papers.authors: Li M, Liu Z, Shen Y, Li Q, Wen K, Gu X et al.
papers.abstract:
Schisandrin B (Sch B), a principal bioactive lignan derived from Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. exhibits diverse pharmacological activities. This traditional Chinese medicine possesses therapeutic value for treating symptoms such as palpitations, shortness of breath, and a faint, nearly imperceptible pulse caused by deficiency of both qi and yin.
This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of Sch B on platelet activation and thrombosis, employing a combination of network pharmacology, molecular docking, and comprehensive in vitro and in vivo functional assays.
Platelet aggregation and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) release were assessed using a lumi-aggregometer. Flow cytometry was used to evaluate Sch B's effects on P-selectin expression and integrin αIIbβ3 activation. Platelet adhesion, spreading, and clot retraction assays were performed to analyze outside-in signaling. Potential targets and signaling pathways of Sch B were predicted through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and these predictions were further investigated using western blot analysis. In vivo, the effects of Sch B on thrombus formation were evaluated using murine models.
Sch B significantly suppressed platelet aggregation, granule release, adhesion, spreading, P-selectin expression, and PAC-1 binding. Western blot further analysis revealed that Sch B reduced the phosphorylation of key signaling molecules, such as Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), AKT, Extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), P38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (P38 MAPK), Talin1, and β3 integrin. In a mesenteric arterial thrombosis model induced by ferric chloride (FeCl3), Sch B significantly prolonged the time to stable thrombus formation. However, it did not significantly effect coagulation parameters or tail-bleeding time in mice.
Sch B inhibits platelet activation by interfering with the PI3K/AKT/ERK-Talin signaling pathway, thereby attenuating thrombus formation. This supports its potential as an antiplatelet agent with a favorable safety profile.

papers.title: Platycodon Decoction alleviates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease associated inflammation with potential dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.
papers.authors: Luan H, Yu M, Wang T, Ji H, Tseng Y
papers.abstract:
The traditional Chinese medicine formula Platycodon Decoction (PD) is known to be effective to alleviate respiratory system-related symptoms, its effect and integrated mechanism for treating COPD requires elucidation.
This study aims to systematically address the pharmocology of PD in treating COPD through analyzing how PD inhibiting the intracellular inflammatory pathway and intercellular interactions.
PD composition was ascertained via LC-MS/MS. PD-induced organ damage was assessed through an acute toxicity test. Following the intervention of PD, body weight, lung index, sputum volume, pulmonary function, expression of inflammatory factors, pulmonary tissue injury, mucus secretion, and MUC5AC expression of the COPD-modeled mice were measured. PD's impacts on the levels of inflammatory factors, cellular activity, proliferation, cell cycle, reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and inter-cellular communication were assessed through Beas-2b human bronchus epithelial cells and THP-1 human macrophage. The PD-associated, COPD relevant inflammatory pathways were analyzed through network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics and then verified through Western blots. The involved cells for cell receptor identified by network pharmacology was analyzed by single-cell sequencing and verified by molecular dynamics and Western blot.
The acute toxicity assessment provided preliminary evidence of PD tolerability under the tested conditions. Fifty compounds were identified in PD. Animal experiments demonstrated that PD can decrease the inflammatory levels and alleviate excessive mucus secretion in mice. In vitro cell experiments indicated that PD can efficiently abate inflammation and oxidative stress within the COPD-related airway microenvironment and diminish epithelial-macrophage interactions. Integration of single-cell and network pharmacology analyses identified ADGRE5 as a candidate receptor that may mediate epithelial-macrophage interactions. PD treatment reduced PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and was accompanied by decreased ADGRE5 expression. Computational analyses suggested a potential interaction between platycodin D and ADGRE5.
PD alleviates inflammation in COPD, potentially involving dual-layer regulation of PI3K/AKT/NLRP3 signaling and ADGRE5-mediated intercellular interactions.

papers.title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.authors: Li Q, Liu Y, Zhou Z, Huang Y, Deng L, Ye Y
papers.abstract:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated.
To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation.
The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF.
HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA.
SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

papers.title: Herbal-Cake-Separated Moxibustion Ameliorates Renal Fibrosis and Associated Bone Injury in Rats via the TGF-β1/Smad Signaling Pathway.
papers.authors: Yin C, Dong Q, Ai M, Ning J, Wang S, Jiang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis is the main pathological basis for chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression and is often accompanied by decreased bone density and impaired bone microstructure. The TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway may be a common intervention target for kidney and bone injury. This study evaluated the effects of herbal-cake-separated moxibustion (HCSM) on renal fibrosis and bone damage in CKD rats and explored its potential mechanism. CKD was induced by adenine gavage combined with a high-protein diet. Successfully modeled rats were randomly assigned to model, HCSM, and SIS3 groups (n = 6 each), with an additional control group (n = 6). The control and model groups received no intervention. The HCSM group received treatment at Pishu (BL20) and Shenshu (BL23), whereas the SIS3 group received intraperitoneal SIS3 (2.5 mg/kg every 2 days). Treatment comprised three 12-day courses separated by 2-day intervals. Renal injury was assessed by kidney function, kidney index, and histopathology. Western blotting measured TGF-β1, Smad2/3, p-Smad2/3, and BMP-7 expression, and micro-computed tomography assessed femoral bone density and microstructure. Compared with controls, model rats showed significantly increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum creatinine (Scr), and kidney index (p < 0.0001); marked renal fibrosis; increased TGF-β1, p-Smad2/3, and Smad2/3; decreased BMP-7; reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular number; and increased trabecular separation. Compared with the model group, HCSM and SIS3 improved renal function and histopathology, increased BMD and trabecular number, reduced trabecular separation, suppressed TGF-β1/Smad signaling, and increased BMP-7 expression. These findings indicate that HCSM may improve renal fibrosis and associated bone damage by enhancing BMP-7 expression and inhibiting TGF-β1/Smad signaling.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture following microsurgical neurorrhaphy: functional and histological outcomes in a rat model.
papers.authors: Gonçalves FGA, Chao LW, Sampaio ECDF, Domingos Neto AA, Abud LR, Hazan ASB et al.
papers.abstract:
This study evaluated electroacupuncture (EA) as adjunctive therapy after peripheral nerve repair in a rat model.
Male Wistar rats underwent right sciatic nerve transection followed by neurorrhaphy and were randomized into EA or control groups. EA was performed twice weekly for 12 weeks. Sensory and motor recovery were assessed by nociceptive, mechanical, thermal, and sciatic functional index tests. Histological analyses evaluated Schwann cell and vascular densities, and gastrocnemius muscle weight was measured at euthanasia.
Sensory recovery was significantly greater in the EA group, with higher pain (3 [3-3.75] versus 2 [1-2], p = 0.02), pressure (2.5 [1.25-3] versus 0 [0-1], p = 0.009), and thermal sensitivity scores (2 [2-2.75] versus 0 [0-0], p = 0.02). Motor recovery and vascular density did not differ between groups. Distal Schwann cell density was significantly higher in the EA group (73.5 [67.4-74.1] versus 34.7 [34.5-38.4], p = 0.014). Gastrocnemius muscle weight was reduced in operated limbs in both groups, without intergroup differences.
EA improved sensory recovery and increased distal Schwann cell density, supporting its potential as an adjunctive therapy after peripheral nerve repair.

papers.title: The Pt(IV) complexes of norcantharidin axial-modulated by carboxylic acid ligand: Synthesis, characterization, in vitro/in vivo anticancer efficacy and hypoxic activity.
papers.authors: Ding TY, Li DM, Bi XB, Luo SS, Huang Y, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract: Norcantharidin (NCTD), a semi-synthetic derivative of cantharidin from the animal-derived traditional Chinese medicine Cantharides, was selected as a potential functional anticancer ligand. Then three new Pt(IV) complexes (Pt-NCTD-bu, Pt-NCTD-pe, Pt-NCTD-he) were designed as a homologous series to evaluate how increasing axial chain length affects lipophilicity and anticancer efficacy. The axial carboxylate ligands were employed to modulate lipophilicity and coordination stability. These complexes exhibited stronger cytotoxicity against the most sensitive A2780 cells than cisplatin, with the order of potency following he > pe > bu, correlating with increasing lipophilicity and cellular uptake. All three complexes also effectively suppressed colony formation. They also overcame cisplatin resistance in A2780/CDDP cells. Mechanistically, they could release active Pt(II) and NCTD via GSH-mediated reduction, inducing ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage and cell apoptosis. Especially, under intracellular hypoxia condition, Pt-NCTD-he showed the highest oxygen-independent cytotoxicity. In vivo, Pt-NCTD-he (20 mg/kg) more effectively suppressed tumor growth in A2780 xenografts than cisplatin, with a 70.0% inhibition rate. Pt-NCTD-he was found to mainly distribute in the liver, indicating that a higher lipophilicity is conducive to better anticancer activity. Pt-NCTD-he also showed satisfactory pharmacokinetic properties, with a longer elimination half-life (1.3 h) than cisplatin (ca. 0.5 h). This work highlights the rational design of Pt(IV) complexes by integrating natural medicinal ingredients, providing a promising strategy for the new generation of Pt(IV)-based complexes as anticancer prodrugs.

papers.title: Beneficial effects of the decoction from Ximenia americana stem barks on sodium monoiodoacetate-induced osteoarthritis in rats.
papers.authors: Assreuy AMS, Holanda BF, Nascimento FGDS, Araujo DF, Ferreira JKA, Pereira MG et al.
papers.abstract: Barks of Ximenia americana L. (Olacaceae), or wild plum, are used in folk medicine to treat inflammatory and painful conditions, in line with experimental studies that have demonstrated its anti-inflammatory effect. This study performed the chemical characterisation and investigated the anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects of the decoction rich in carbohydrates/polyphenols from X. americana stem barks (DC-Xa) on experimental osteoarthritis. Animals received monoiodoacetate in the tibiotarsal joints and were treated daily with DC-Xa (100 mg/kg/day p.o.) during 28 days for evaluation of inflammatory, nociceptive, oxidative, histopathological and functional parameters. HPLC identified gallic acid as the main constituent (8.49%). DC-Xa reduced peripheral (59%) and central (65%) nociception; oedema (65%); leukocytes (60%); TNF-α (24%), IL-1β (42%), IL-6 (21%); malondialdehyde (66%); nitrite (13%) and cartilage damage (64%); increased GSH (49%) and SOD activity (47%) and ameliorated mobility. DC-Xa attenuates inflammation, nociception, oxidative and cartilage damage and restores functional capacity in experimental osteoarthritis.

papers.title: Astragali Radix-Curcumae Rhizoma synergistically potentiates 5-fluorouracil antitumor efficacy in colorectal cancer by disrupting DNA repair-cell cycle coordination.
papers.authors: Wang S, Huang K, Cheng Y, Sun C, Wang K, He Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Astragali Radix (HQ) and Curcumae Rhizoma (EZ), collectively termed AC, are commonly used as an herb pair in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for colorectal cancer (CRC). Although AC has been used as an adjuvant to chemotherapy, the molecular basis by which it enhances the efficacy of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) remains incompletely defined.
The antitumor effect of AC alone and in combination with 5-FU was evaluated in a HCT116 xenograft mouse model and in CRC cell lines with different genetic backgrounds. Potential systemic toxicity was assessed using serum biochemical markers. Transcriptomic changes induced by AC were analyzed by RNA sequencing and integrated with network pharmacology and The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) (GSE17536, GSE17537, GSE41258, GSE20916). Key targets were validated by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Cell viability, drug interaction, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution and DNA damage were assessed using CCK-8 assays, Synergy Finder analysis, flow cytometry, and γ-H2AX staining. Bioavailable AC-derived constituents were characterized by UPLC-QTOF-MS, and candidate active compounds were further evaluated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, and functional validation.
AC potentiated the antitumor efficacy of 5-FU in vivo and did not exacerbate 5-FU-associated hepatic or renal biochemical toxicity under the tested conditions. In vitro, AC-containing serum extracts inhibited CRC cell viability, induced reversible G2/M-phase arrest, and enhanced 5-FU sensitivity in HCT116, CT26, and HCT15 cells. AC treatment caused limited early apoptosis, whereas delayed apoptosis was observed after prolonged exposure, suggesting that cell-cycle arrest represents the primary early response. RNA-seq and integrative analyses showed that AC suppressed pathways associated with DNA replication, mismatch repair, ribosome biogenesis, and cell-cycle progression. AC downregulated key regulators involved in cell-cycle control, DNA repair, and stress-survival signaling, including PLK1, CDK1, CCNB1, CDC25A, c-JUN, MSH2, BRCA1, and p-AKT. Combination treatment further increased γ-H2AX accumulation and reduced cell-cycle regulatory proteins. Functional validation indicated that c-JUN overexpression partially attenuated AC-mediated 5-FU sensitization, whereas pharmacological AKT inhibition partially mimicked the sensitizing effect of AC. Among the serum-exposed constituents, Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin were identified as bioavailable active compounds that partially recapitulated the effects of AC by inducing G2/M-phase arrest and enhancing the antiproliferative activity of 5-FU. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and CETSA supported their target engagement with cell-cycle regulators, particularly CCNB1 and CDK1.
AC enhances the therapeutic efficacy of 5-FU in CRC by weakening DNA repair-cell-cycle coordination and stress-survival signaling, thereby increasing 5-FU-induced DNA damage and promoting cell-cycle arrest. Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin may represent important bioavailable contributors to this chemosensitizing effect, although the complete AC extract likely acts through multi-component and multi-target mechanisms. These findings provide mechanistic support for the use of AC as an adjunctive strategy to improve 5-FU-based chemotherapy in CRC.

papers.title: Methyl jasmonate induces the biosynthesis and accumulation of triterpenoid saponins in Polygala tenuifolia hairy roots.
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.authors: Ji H, Yang B, Lai N, Zhang L, Yang Y, Zhao X et al.
papers.abstract: Polygala tenuifolia Willd. is an important medicinal plant widely applied in traditional Chinese medicine. Its pharmacological activities are primarily derived from triterpenoid saponins and other specialized metabolites. Nevertheless, the regulatory mechanisms governing methyl jasmonate (MeJA)-triggered accumulation of bioactive constituents in P. tenuifolia remain poorly characterized. In this study, to evaluate corresponding changes in biomass and characteristic metabolite production, hairy root cultures of P. tenuifolia were subjected to MeJA treatment at concentrations spanning 0 to 400µM over a 1-6 day period. MeJA modulated hairy root growth and secondary metabolite accumulation in a concentration-dependent and time-dependent manner. Compared with the control group, the contents of onjisaponin B and polygalasaponin III increased by 1.81-fold and 2.60-fold, respectively, following treatment with 50µM MeJA for 3 days. A total of 447 differentially expressed transcription factors (TFs) that belonged to 64 families were identified through transcriptome analysis. MeJA suppressed the expression of most TF families, whereas the NAC family exhibited a global upregulation trend. The above results indicated that MeJA activated transcriptional reprogramming of secondary-metabolism-associated genes via targeted regulation of specific TFs. Correlation analysis involving ten key enzyme genes and six characteristic metabolites demonstrated that the majority of biosynthetic genes were positively associated with bioactive metabolite levels. Of these genes, UGT74B1 and UGT73B2 showed strong positive correlations with multiple saponin components; CYP94A2 served as a critical node responsible for oxidative modification. In contrast, MK and HDS displayed negative correlations with saponins, which suggested precursor competition across distinct terpenoid pathways. As indicated by RT-qPCR validation for ten candidate biosynthetic genes, MeJA time-dependently upregulated key genes participating in the MVA/MEP pathways, squalene cyclization, CYP450-mediated oxidation, and UGT-catalyzed glycosylation, thereby facilitating precursor supply and subsequent structural modification. Accordingly, triterpenoid saponin biosynthesis and accumulation in P. tenuifolia hairy roots were enhanced. This study offers fresh understanding of the molecular basis underlying MeJA-modulated secondary metabolism in P. tenuifolia, and identifies candidate genes applicable to metabolic engineering for elevating yields of bioactive compounds in hairy root cultures.

papers.title: Application of Immersive and Semi-Immersive Extended Reality Training Systems in Acupuncture Education: Scoping Review.
papers.authors: Jeong H, Park H, Ahn J, Kim KH, Lee H, Bang T et al.
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture training requires precise acupoint localization and needle control, yet peer-to-peer practice raises safety concerns and physical phantoms offer limited anatomical fidelity. Extended reality (XR) is increasingly used in health professions education, but immersive and semi-immersive XR training systems for acupuncture have not been mapped.
This scoping review aimed to map the applications, hardware modalities, and reported technical and educational outcomes of immersive and semi-immersive XR training systems in acupuncture education.
This review followed the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) and the five-stage scoping review framework of Arksey and O'Malley, as refined by Levac and colleagues. On September 19, 2026, we searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, CNKI, RISS, ScienceOn, and OASIS. No language or date restrictions were applied. Backward and forward citation searching supplemented the database search. Eligible sources were peer-reviewed original studies or full conference papers describing virtual reality (VR; either fully immersive [IVR] or semi-immersive [SIVR]), augmented reality (AR), or mixed reality (MR) systems for acupuncture training. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted the study design, hardware, training task, and outcomes. Each study was assigned an evidence tier.
Of 6176 records, 3378 were screened after removal of duplicates and ineligible document types, 80 reports were assessed in full text, and 26 studies were included (25 from databases and 1 from citation searching). Most studies came from East Asia (25/26, 96.2%), mainly China (n=18), and 20 (76.9%) were published between 2020 and 2026. Systems used VR (n=15), AR (n=5), or MR (n=6); 19 were IVR and 7 were SIVR. Training tasks addressed acupoint localization (n=13), needling skills (n=11), and clinical reasoning (n=2). Localization errors were reported with different metrics and were not directly comparable across systems. In a randomized comparison, a VR group scored higher on practical skills than a conventional instruction group (32.52, SD 2.28 vs 28.62, SD 2.77 points; P<.001). In an MR simulator with depth-responsive vibrotactile feedback active in both sessions, mean depth error decreased from 6.41 mm in the first practice session to 3.58 mm in the second. Of the 26 studies, 7 used a comparative design; the rest were technical validation (n=6), system development (n=10), or case and survey reports (n=3). Reported barriers included headset weight, narrow field of view, tracking instability, and limited tactile fidelity.
Immersive and semi-immersive XR systems for acupuncture training have been developed mainly for acupoint localization and needling. Randomized comparisons reported higher test scores than conventional instruction, but most evidence came from system development reports and small feasibility studies. Randomized trials comparing XR-based and conventional training on objective localization and needling outcomes are needed before these systems are adopted for competency assessment.

summary.methods: PRISMA-ScR에 따라 여러 데이터베이스를 검색한 범위 문헌고찰로, 침구 훈련용 VR·AR·MR 시스템의 설계, 하드웨어, 과제와 결과를 두 평가자가 선별·정리하였다.

papers.title: Thermographic outcomes of auricular laser acupuncture and auricular seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain: an exploratory nonrandomized, nonconcurrent comparison.
papers.authors: Quadros G, Lo Schiavo Arisawa EA, Soares LE
papers.abstract:
Compare pain, quality of life, and cutaneous temperature changes within predefined anterior, lateral, and posterior shoulder regions of interest between auricular laser acupuncture and seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain.
This exploratory, nonrandomized, open-label study enrolled 20 adults aged 60-90 years, allocated by order of entry to consecutive, nonconcurrent cohorts of auricular laser acupuncture (n = 10) or seed acupressure (n = 10), treated twice weekly for five weeks. VAS, McGill, SF-36, and thermography were assessed before the first (A1) and fifth sessions (A2) and after the tenth (A3) and analyzed using linear mixed-effects models.
From A1 to A3, VAS decreased by - 2.70 points in Laser (95% CI - 4.37 to - 1.03) and - 2.50 in Seed (95% CI - 4.17 to - 0.83); the between-group difference was - 0.20 points (Laser - Seed; 95% CI - 2.54 to 2.14). Selected McGill and SF-36 outcomes changed; McGill affective A1-to-A2 change differed between groups (Laser - Seed: -2.70; 95% CI - 4.86 to - 0.55; p = 0.017). Anterior thermal range (ΔT) showed a TIME × GROUP interaction (p = 0.007); the A1-to-A3 between-group difference was - 1.941 °C (Seed - Laser; 95% CI - 3.097 to - 0.785), although Seed ΔT was higher at baseline (+ 1.496 °C; 95% CI 0.607 to 2.385). Lateral ΔT showed a TIME effect (p = 0.033); posterior ΔT showed none.
Clinical outcomes improved over time without evidence of differential changes between interventions. Thermography identified region-specific ΔT trajectories, warranting further investigation as a complementary method.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07010627.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence models Traditional Chinese Medicine principles to integrate with biomedicine.
papers.authors: Li H, Cheng X, Huang Z, Luo J, Xu Q, Zhao Q et al.
papers.abstract: Using 26,339 model-eligible Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula records, we trained an autoencoder following TCM's compression-expansion logic to learn the TCM embedding space (TCM-ES), quantifying symptom-pattern-formula mappings. TCM-ES aligns with conventional TCM principles not used in training. Biomedical entities were mapped post hoc into the fixed space, supporting formula prediction, retrospective clinical analyses, and exploratory therapeutic prioritization.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
papers.authors: Qi F, Cai P, Zhao L, Wang M
papers.abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

papers.title: Nighttime Symptom Burden in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Qualitative Study.
papers.authors: Miller S, Germack HD, Bell M, Feigler N, Legg R, Henderson K et al.
papers.abstract:
Nighttime symptoms are clinically important but understudied in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). This study explored patients' perceptions of nighttime symptoms, their effects on daily life, and symptom-management strategies.
Thirty U.S. adults with COPD and moderate-to-high symptom burden (COPD Assessment Test score ≥10), without hospitalization or emergency department visits for severe exacerbation during the previous year, participated in semi-structured interviews. All participants received single-inhaler dual or triple maintenance therapy and completed the 7-item COPD and Asthma Sleep Impact Scal. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and thematically analyzed using the Symptom Management Theory framework.
Participants (median age 63; 60% female; 90% White) reported a high burden of nighttime symptoms and sleep disruption (87% severely impacted based on CASIS). Participants described a pronounced nighttime symptom experience, most frequently shortness of breath, mucus/phlegm production, coughing, and difficulty staying asleep or frequent awakenings. A range of symptom management strategies was reported, including behavioral adaptations (routines, avoidance of technology, sleep hygiene), pharmacological management (antidepressants, sleep medications, rescue inhalers), and complementary and integrative approaches (meditation, acupuncture, relaxation techniques). Nighttime symptom outcomes extended beyond sleep disruption. Participants reported significant daytime consequences, including fatigue and impaired concentration. These effects contributed to activity avoidance and limitations in social participation.
Among symptomatic patients receiving single-inhaler dual or triple maintenance therapy, nighttime COPD symptoms were commonly reported and were associated with substantial physical, emotional, and functional impacts. The findings support further consideration of nighttime symptoms in clinical assessment and individualized COPD management.

papers.title: From Physiological Spaces to Cognitive Health: A New Perspective on Combined Acupuncture and Chinese Herbal Medicine for Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.authors: Zhang K
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an escalating global health challenge. Although the target-centric paradigm focusing on targets such as β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, and neuroinflammation has advanced our understanding of AD, translated therapies remain limited in reversing disease progression. Viewing the brain through the lens of physiological spaces offers an alternative framework for re-evaluating AD pathogenesis. Under this theoretical model, the body comprises both physical structures ("entities") and fluid-filled interstitial networks ("spaces"), with the latter facilitating metabolic transport, waste clearance, and intercellular signaling. Cerebral perivascular spaces, the extracellular space, and the glymphatic pathway represent specialized cranial interstitial networks. Fluid dynamic impairment within these spatial domains may serve as an upstream trigger for downstream Aβ aggregation, tau pathology, and neuroinflammatory cascades. Combining acupuncture with Chinese herbal medicine may restore fluid homeostasis and spatial patency across these networks. In a preliminary exploration study of 11 patients with mild-to-moderate AD, combined intervention showed encouraging trends toward improving cognitive performance and modulating relevant fluid biomarkers. This spatial perspective provides a complementary target for future AD disease-modifying strategies.
